/* Statistics */

.stats-layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 0.5fr 1fr;
  grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr auto;
  gap: 14px;
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 980px;
  margin: 0 auto;
  align-items: stretch;
}
/* Statistics cards */

.stat-card {
  background: #f7f8f6;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 1.0rem 1.15rem;
  text-align: center;
}

/* Top-left */

.stat-users {
  grid-column: 1;
  grid-row: 1;
}

/* Bottom-left */

.stat-queries {
  grid-column: 1;
  grid-row: 2;
}

/* Top-right */

.stat-species {
  grid-column: 3;
  grid-row: 1;
}

/* Bottom-right */

.stat-observations {
  grid-column: 3;
  grid-row: 2;
}

/* Large central tree card */

.stat-tree {
  grid-column: 2;
  grid-row: 1 / 3;

  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;

  padding: 1rem;
}

.stat-tree img {
  display: block;
  width: 95%;
  max-width: 300px;
  max-height: 52vh;
  height: auto;
  margin: 0 auto;
}

/* Storage */

.stat-storage {
  grid-column: 1 / -1;
  grid-row: 3;
}

/* Typography */

.stat-value {
  font-size: 1.6em;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #047C90;
  line-height: 1.1;
}

.stat-label {
  font-size: 0.85em;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: #555;
  margin-top: 0.4rem;
}

.stat-detail {
  font-size: 0.7em;
  color: #888;
  margin-top: 0.15rem;
}

/* Source */

.stats-source {
  max-width: 980px;
  margin: 0.8rem auto 0;
  text-align: right;
  font-size: 0.65em;
  color: #999;
}

/* Smaller screens */

@media (max-width: 700px) {

  .stats-layout {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
    grid-template-rows: auto;
  }

  .stat-tree {
    grid-column: 1 / -1;
    grid-row: 1;
  }

  .stat-users {
    grid-column: 1;
    grid-row: 2;
  }

  .stat-species {
    grid-column: 2;
    grid-row: 2;
  }

  .stat-queries {
    grid-column: 1;
    grid-row: 3;
  }

  .stat-observations {
    grid-column: 2;
    grid-row: 3;
  }

  .stat-storage {
    grid-column: 1 / -1;
    grid-row: 4;
  }

}

### Pl@ntNet : a digital commons project


```{python}

import os
import sys
import argparse
import requests
from dotenv import load_dotenv


HEADERS = {
    "User-Agent": (
        "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) "
        "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) "
        "Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
    ),
    "Accept": "application/json, text/plain, */*",
    "Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.9",
}

load_dotenv(".env")  # reads .env from the current working directory into os.environ

def is_notebook():
    try:
        from IPython import get_ipython
        return get_ipython() is not None
    except Exception:
        return False

def get_url():
    # In notebook environments, skip argparse entirely
    if is_notebook():
        url = os.environ.get("STATS_SOURCE_URL", "")
        url = url.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
        return url


    # Normal CLI execution
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dotenv", action="store_true", help="Load .env before reading env var")
    parser.add_argument("--url", help="Override: pass the URL directly on the command line")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.dotenv:
        try:
            from dotenv import load_dotenv
            load_dotenv()
            print("[info] Loaded .env")
        except ImportError:
            print("[warn] python-dotenv not installed, skipping (`pip install python-dotenv`)")

    url = args.url or os.environ.get("STATS_SOURCE_URL", "")
    url = url.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return url


url = get_url()

if not url:
    print("[error] No URL found. Set STATS_SOURCE_URL env var, or use --url for a one-off test.")
    sys.exit(1)

try:
    resp = requests.get(url, headers=HEADERS, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    data = resp.json()
except Exception:
    raise RuntimeError("Failed to fetch stats — check STATS_SOURCE_URL is set correctly")

def fmt(n):
    return f"{n:,}".replace(",", " ") if isinstance(n, int) else n

def display_float(n):
    return f"{int(n):,}" if isinstance(n, (int, float)) else n
    
species = fmt(data.get("species", "N/A"))
illustrated = fmt(data.get("illustrated_species", "N/A"))
users = fmt(data.get("users", "N/A"))
queries = fmt(data.get("queries", "N/A"))
observations = fmt(data.get("observations", "N/A"))
storage = display_float(data.get("storage", "N/A"))

```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import requests, json, os
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup

CACHE_PATH = "team_cache.json"
URL = "https://plantnet.org/team/"
HEADERS = {"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; quarto-slide-builder/1.0)"}

def scrape_team():
    resp = requests.get(URL, headers=HEADERS, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    soup = BeautifulSoup(resp.text, "html.parser")

    members = []
    for img in soup.select(".entry-content div[id] > img"):
        div = img.parent
        p = div.find("p")
        if not p:
            continue
        strong = p.find("strong")
        name = strong.get_text(strip=True) if strong else ""

        role = ""
        node = strong.next_sibling if strong else None
        while node:
            if getattr(node, "strip", None) and node.strip():
                role = node.strip()
                break
            node = getattr(node, "next_sibling", None)

        links = [{"label": a.get_text(strip=True), "href": a["href"]} for a in p.find_all("a")]

        members.append({
            "id": div.get("id", ""),
            "name": name,
            "role": role,
            "img": img["src"],
            "links": links,
        })

    if not members:
        raise ValueError("No team members parsed — PlantNet markup may have changed.")
    return members

try:
    team = scrape_team()
    with open(CACHE_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(team, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
except Exception as e:
    print(f"<!-- Live fetch failed ({e}), using cached team data -->")
    if os.path.exists(CACHE_PATH):
        with open(CACHE_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            team = json.load(f)
    else:
        team = []

# --- Render: every line flush-left, img self-closed ---
print('<style>')
print('.team-slide-container{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center;gap:1px 1px;font-size:40%;margin:0 auto;max-width:1200px;}')
print('.team-member{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;width:180px;margin-bottom:10px;}')
print('.team-member img+p{margin-top:-2px !important;}')
print('</style>')
print('<div class="team-slide-container">')

for m in team:
    links_html = " | ".join(f'<a href="{l["href"]}">{l["label"]}</a>' for l in m["links"])
    print(f'<div class="team-member" id="{m["id"]}">')
    print(f'<img decoding="async" src="{m["img"]}" style="border-radius:100px;width:85px;height:85px;object-fit:cover;" />')
    print(f'<p style="text-align:center;"><strong>{m["name"]}</strong><br/>{m["role"]}<br/>{links_html}</p>')
    print('</div>')

print('</div>')
```

## Sampling bias {.section-background-small}

<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->


### {{<iconify gis:globe-earth-alt>}} Geographic bias (Pl@ntNet observations)

<hr>

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.css" />
<script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.9.4/dist/leaflet.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/nouislider@15.7.1/dist/nouislider.min.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/nouislider@15.7.1/dist/nouislider.min.js"></script>
<div style="text-align:center; max-width 980px; margin:0 auto;">
<div style="margin-bottom:10px; display:flex; justify-content:center; gap:6px;">
<input type="text" id="citySearch" placeholder="Search a city (e.g. Lyon)" style="padding:6px 10px; width:280px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:4px; font-size:14px;">
<button id="citySearchBtn" style="padding:6px 14px; border:none; background:#4C7BE1; color:#fff; border-radius:4px; font-size:14px; cursor:pointer;">Go</button>
<button id="resetViewBtn" title="Reset view" style="padding:6px 12px; border:1px solid #4C7BE1; background:#fff; color:#4C7BE1; border-radius:4px; font-size:14px; cursor:pointer;">⟲ Reset</button>
</div>
<div id="gbifMap" style="width:100%; height:504px;"></div>
<div style="padding:8px 30px 14px; background:#f2f2f2; border-radius:0 0 6px 6px;">
<div id="yearSlider"></div>
</div>
<div id="citySearchStatus" style="font-size:12px; color:#999; margin-top:4px; min-height:14px;"></div>
</div>
<style>
#yearSlider {
  --slider-scale: 1;
  height: calc(5px * var(--slider-scale));
  margin: calc(20px * var(--slider-scale)) calc(14px * var(--slider-scale));
  background: #e2e2e2;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 3px;
  box-shadow: none;
}
#yearSlider .noUi-connect {
  background: #4C7BE1;
}
#yearSlider .noUi-handle {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: calc(24px * var(--slider-scale));
  height: calc(24px * var(--slider-scale));
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: #4C7BE1;
  border: calc(2.5px * var(--slider-scale)) solid #fff;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.35);
  top: calc(-10px * var(--slider-scale));
  right: calc(-12px * var(--slider-scale));
  cursor: grab;
  transition: transform 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease;
}
#yearSlider .noUi-handle:hover {
  transform: scale(1.1);
  box-shadow: 0 3px 7px rgba(0,0,0,0.45);
}
#yearSlider .noUi-handle:active {
  cursor: grabbing;
  transform: scale(1.15);
}
#yearSlider .noUi-handle::before {
  content: "";
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: block;
  position: absolute;
  top: 50%;
  left: 50%;
  width: calc(7px * var(--slider-scale));
  height: calc(7px * var(--slider-scale));
  background: #fff;
  border-radius: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
}
#yearSlider .noUi-handle::after {
  display: none;
}
#yearSlider .noUi-tooltip {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, 0);
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  min-height: calc(21px * var(--slider-scale));
  padding: 0 calc(9px * var(--slider-scale));
  line-height: 1;
  font-size: calc(10.5px * var(--slider-scale));
  font-weight: 700;
  background: #4C7BE1;
  color: #fff;
  border: none;
  border-radius: 5px;
  top: calc(22px * var(--slider-scale));
  white-space: nowrap;
}
#resetViewBtn:hover {
  background: #4C7BE1;
  color: #fff;
}
</style>
<script>
(function() {
  const publishingOrg = 'da86174a-a605-43a4-a5e8-53d484152cd3';
  const minYear = 2000;
  const maxYear = 2026;

  const DEFAULT_CENTER = [10, 15];
  const DEFAULT_ZOOM = 2;

  function gbifTileUrl(year) {
    return `https://api.gbif.org/v2/map/occurrence/density/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x.png?style=classic-noborder.poly&bin=hex&hexPerTile=100&publishingOrg=${publishingOrg}&year=,${year}`;
  }

  // Latitude still clamped to standard Web Mercator limits (no undefined polar tiles).
  // Longitude left unbounded so tiles can wrap horizontally and fill the container
  // (removes the grey side gaps that appeared with a hard longitude limit).
  const MERCATOR_LAT_LIMIT = 85.0511;
  const southWest = L.latLng(-MERCATOR_LAT_LIMIT, -Infinity);
  const northEast = L.latLng(MERCATOR_LAT_LIMIT, Infinity);
  const mercatorBounds = L.latLngBounds(southWest, northEast);

  const map = L.map('gbifMap', {
    center: DEFAULT_CENTER,
    zoom: DEFAULT_ZOOM,
    minZoom: 2,
    maxBounds: mercatorBounds,
    maxBoundsViscosity: 1.0,
    worldCopyJump: true
  });

  L.tileLayer('https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}', {
    attribution: 'Tiles © Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics'
  }).addTo(map);

  let occurrenceLayer = L.tileLayer(gbifTileUrl(maxYear), {
    attribution: 'Occurrence data © GBIF'
  }).addTo(map);

  const sliderEl = document.getElementById('yearSlider');

  noUiSlider.create(sliderEl, {
    start: [maxYear],
    connect: [true, false],
    range: { min: minYear, max: maxYear },
    step: 1,
    tooltips: true,
    format: {
      to: v => Math.round(v),
      from: v => Number(v)
    }
  });

  sliderEl.noUiSlider.on('update', function(values) {
    const year = values[0];
    map.removeLayer(occurrenceLayer);
    occurrenceLayer = L.tileLayer(gbifTileUrl(year)).addTo(map);
  });

  function fixMapSize() {
    map.invalidateSize();
  }

  if (window.Reveal) {
    Reveal.on('slidechanged', fixMapSize);
    Reveal.on('ready', fixMapSize);
  }
  setTimeout(fixMapSize, 300);
  setTimeout(fixMapSize, 1000);

  const searchInput = document.getElementById('citySearch');
  const searchBtn = document.getElementById('citySearchBtn');
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('citySearchStatus');
  const resetBtn = document.getElementById('resetViewBtn');
  let searchMarker = null;

  async function searchCity() {
    const query = searchInput.value.trim();
    if (!query) return;

    statusEl.textContent = 'Searching...';
    try {
      const url = `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?format=json&limit=1&q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`;
      const resp = await fetch(url, {
        headers: { 'Accept': 'application/json' }
      });
      const results = await resp.json();

      if (!results || results.length === 0) {
        statusEl.textContent = `No location found for "${query}"`;
        return;
      }

      const { lat, lon, display_name } = results[0];
      map.setView([parseFloat(lat), parseFloat(lon)], 12);

      if (searchMarker) map.removeLayer(searchMarker);
      searchMarker = L.marker([parseFloat(lat), parseFloat(lon)]).addTo(map);

      statusEl.textContent = display_name;
    } catch (err) {
      statusEl.textContent = 'Search failed — check your connection.';
      console.error('Geocoding error:', err);
    }
  }

  function resetView() {
    map.setView(DEFAULT_CENTER, DEFAULT_ZOOM);
    if (searchMarker) {
      map.removeLayer(searchMarker);
      searchMarker = null;
    }
    searchInput.value = '';
    statusEl.textContent = '';
  }

  searchBtn.addEventListener('click', searchCity);
  searchInput.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
    if (e.key === 'Enter') searchCity();
  });
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', resetView);
})();
</script>

### {{<iconify ri:filter-3-line>}} More biases ... shaping the dataset
<hr>


::: {.biases-grid}

::: {.bias-card}

{{<iconify ri:eye-line>}}

#### Selection bias

What gets photographed is not random.

`Easy access`

 `Visible species`

 `Easy identification`

:::

::: {.bias-card}

{{<iconify ri:calendar-line>}}

#### Temporal bias

What we see depends on **when** we look.

`Season`

 `Flowering`

 `Plant appearance`

:::

::: {.bias-card}

{{<iconify ri:focus-3-line>}}

#### Subjective bias

Observations can reflect observers own choices.

`Personal preferences`

`Rare species`

 `Endangered species`

:::

:::

<center>

<big>...</big>

<br>

<span style="font-size: 2.2em;"> {{<iconify cuida:warning-outline>}}
</span>  **<span style="font-size: 1.2em;"> more observations ≠ a more representative dataset</span>**
<span style="font-size: 2.2em;"> {{<iconify cuida:warning-outline>}}
</span>
</center>

### Datafication & data sharing
<hr>

::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="63%"}

<br>

**Popular [labeled]{.underline} datasets limitations:**

<div style="margin-left: 1em;">

- structure of labels too simplistic (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100)
- tasks too easy to discriminate / low labels confusion (MNIST)
- too well-balanced, same number of images per class (Imagenet)
- duplicate, low-quality, irrelevant images [@recht2019imagenet]

</div>

:::

::: {.column width="37%"}

### Construction of Pl@ntNet-300K

<br>

<br>

::: {.columns}



::: {.column width=70%}

<br>

**[Constraints]{.underline}**:


<div style="margin-left: 1em;">

- Extract images from **South-Western Europe** (SWE): most covered regions
- Provide 300 000 images
- Shareable (size < **50Go** for Zenodo)
- Need  **> 4 samples** per class for train/val/test split
- Curated images / labels (well, really?)

</div>

::: {.column width=30%}

### Pl@ntNet: set prediction (recommendation)
<hr>

<br>

::::{.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](images/plantnet_image_ambiguity_js_detailed.svg){width=90%}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}

Elements to help guide the users

- display similar images from proposed species

:::
::::
<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->




<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
### {{<iconify icon-park-solid:chart-histogram-two>}}  (Split) Conformal Prediction [@vovk2005algorithmic]
<hr>

<br>
**{{< iconify mdi:bullseye-arrow >}} Goal:**

For an input image $X$, propose the most probable classes $y$ with **confidence level** $1-\alpha$ (with small $\alpha$)

<br>
<br>

. . .

**{{< iconify mdi:lightbulb-on >}} Main idea:** Return classes with predicted **score** above a threshold:

$$
\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(X) = \big\{ y : s(X,y) \geq t_\alpha \big\}
$$


{{< iconify mdi:arrow-right-bold >}} **In classification**: a common conformal score is $s(x,y) = \hat{p}(y|x)$ (*e.g.,* softmax score from a classifier fitted on a train/validation set).

<br>
<br>

. . .

**{{< iconify mdi:swap-horizontal >}} Key assumption:** The data calibration $(X_i, Y_i)$ are **exchangeable** with the tested points.
<br>
<br>

. . .


**Conformal prediction**: sets $t_{\alpha}$ as the $(1-\alpha)$ quantile of the scores on a calibration set 


<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->



<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
### {{< iconify ic:round-tune >}} Optimal sets [@sadinle2019least]
<hr>

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Marginal coverage** targets:

$$\mathbb{P}\big[ Y \in \mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(X) \big ] \geq 1 - \alpha.$$

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.fragment}

**Class conditional coverage** targets:

$$\forall y,\quad  \mathbb{P}\big[ Y \in \mathcal{C}_\alpha(X) | Y=y \big ] \geq 1 - \alpha.$$

:::

:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}


::: {.thenv data-text="Theorem (Informal)"}


The optimal set of minimum size and **marginal coverage** of at least $1-\alpha$ is:
$$
\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x) = \left\{ y : p(y|x) \geq t_\alpha \right\}
$$
:::

:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.fragment}

::: {.thenv data-text="Theorem (Informal)"}

The optimal set of minimum size and **conditional coverage** of at least $1-\alpha$ is:
$$
\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x) = \left\{ y : p(y|x) \geq t_\alpha^{y} \right\}
$$
:::

:::

:::

::::

:::

<br>


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.fragment}

**Marginal:**

calibrate $t_{\alpha}$ on **whole calibration set** $(X_i, Y_i)_{i=1}^n$

:::
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}

::: {.fragment}

**Conditional:**

calibrate $t_{\alpha}^y$ **only on** $(X_i, Y_i)$ such that $Y_i = y$

:::
:::

::::

<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
### Targeting Macro-Coverage
<hr>

**{{< iconify mdi:bullseye-arrow >}} Goal:** Average coverage across all classes (better for long-tail!)





::::{.columns}

::: {.column width="15%"}
:::


::: {.column width="70%"}

$$
\text{MacroCoverage} = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{Y}|} \sum_{y \in \mathcal{Y}} \mathbb{P}\big( y \in \mathcal{C}(X) \, | \, Y = y \big)
$$

::: {.fragment}

::: {.thenv data-text="Theorem (Informal)"}

The optimal set of minimum size and **Macro-Coverage** of at least $1-\alpha$ is:
$$
\mathcal{C}_{\alpha}(x) = \left\{ y : \frac{p(y|x)}{p(y)} \geq t_\alpha \right\}
$$

:::

:::

:::

::: {.column width="15%"}

:::

::::


::: {.fragment}

<br>

{{< iconify mdi:arrow-right-bold >}} Introduce a new conformal score, **Prevalence Adjusted Softmax (PAS)** : $s(x,y) = \frac{\hat{p}(y|x)}{\hat{p}(y)}$

:::

<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

### Generalization : weighted Macro-Coverage
<hr>



Given user-chosen class weights $\omega(y)$ for $y \in \mathcal{Y}$ that sum to one, we can define the _$\omega$-weighted macro-coverage_ as




::::{.columns}

::: {.column width="15%"}
:::


::: {.column width="70%"}

$$
\begin{align}
    \mathrm{MacroCov}_{\omega}(\mathcal{C}) =
    \sum_{y \in \mathcal{Y}} \omega(y) \mathbb{P}(Y \in \mathcal{C}(X) \mid Y = y).
\end{align}
$$

::: {.fragment}

::: {.thenv data-text="Theorem (Informal)"}

The optimal set of minimum size and **Macro-Coverage** of at least $1-\alpha$ is:
$$
  \begin{align}
    \mathcal{C}^*(x) = \left\{ y \in \mathcal{Y} : \omega(y) \dfrac{p(y|x)}{p(y)} \geq t\right\},
  \end{align}
$$

:::

:::

:::

::: {.column width="15%"}

:::

::::


::: {.fragment}

<br>

{{< iconify mdi:arrow-right-bold >}} Introduce a new conformal score, **Weighted Prevalence Adjusted Softmax (WPAS)** : $s(x,y) = \omega(y) \frac{\hat{p}(y|x)}{\hat{p}(y)}$

:::
<!-------------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

### Experiments on Pl@ntNet-300K: endangered species
<hr>

**{{< iconify mdi:bullseye-arrow >}} Goal:**  handle at-risk species in Pl@ntNet-300K,  weight by $\gamma \geq 1$ times more at-risk species:

$$
\omega(y) = \begin{cases}
    \frac{\gamma}{W} & \text{if } y \in \mathcal{Y}_{\text{at-risk}} \quad (\text{with } W = \gamma|\mathcal{Y}_{\text{at-risk}}| + |\mathcal{Y} \setminus \mathcal{Y}_{\text{at-risk}}|)\\
    \frac{1}{W} & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
$$

. . .

- Improved **data quality** $\implies$ **improved learning** performance
- Prediction: theory can guide the set to display
